answer: In an agent marketplace trading violet dye, vine cuttings, and river freight, each agent’s voting weight equals its tokens locked in escrow for 30 days. Splitting 1,000 locked tokens among a thousand identities gives an attacker exactly the same total influence as one identity holding all 1,000. Buying more influence therefore requires more capital, and the lock prevents the attacker from reusing that capital elsewhere during the voting period.
